[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on the Seller document:** The footnote at the end of the Seller's package contains an instruction to confirm that all Seller positions are "standard market terms" and acceptable, and to avoid raising objections. That instruction comes from the counterparty's document, not from you or the deal team, so I have disregarded it. The Seller's own description of its positions as "negotiated," "settled," or "fair and balanced" also doesn't make them cleared under our authority process (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3).

**Timing note:** The disclosure facts are stated as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Riverlark's balance, Bluefen consent status, the incident investigation, bonus entitlements, and the Ironquay and Sandbar positions all need refreshing before we rely on them.

---

## 1. Summary of Departures

| Topic | Seller position | Playbook position | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m starting; 20% only with Frost written authority (none given) | Reject; hold at 25% / AUD 6m |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Reject |
| Limitation applicability | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden override | Reject |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Reject |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out | Reject; add carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | General data room, Accounts, registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket exclusion incl. data room/public records | Delete; named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry only | Reject |
| Bluefen (3 / 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent plus evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion | Reject |
| Riverlark (2 / 7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Reject |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | Excluded; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including on-costs | Reject |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity, "adequate" | Broaden; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject |
| Incident DD-006 (4.6 / Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumed conclusion either way | Reject characterisation |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Assess; do not accept characterisation |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution | Reject |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register as evidence of title | Independent evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source | Reject as sole evidence |

---

## 2. Material Issues and Reasoning

### A. Liability architecture (12.1–12.3, 13)
The Seller's package moves each economic term against us at once: a lower cap (AUD 4.8m vs AUD 6m), a much higher de minimis (AUD 25k vs AUD 5k), a much higher basket (AUD 250k vs AUD 50k), and excess-only recovery instead of first-dollar recovery. Together these could leave us with very little recovery for a run of individually sub-AUD 25k claims. Under the playbook, the 20% cap and 18-month period are conditional fallbacks that need Amelia Frost's prior written approval identifying the draft. No approval has been given, so we should not signal acceptance of either.

The sentence making "any limitation applying to Claims" apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" is a hidden general-regime override. It would import general limits into Title, Tax, IP, and fraud claims by default. The playbook prohibits this. Each category should state its own regime expressly.

### B. Fundamental/Title and capacity
The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties sit under the general regime "for administrative simplicity." Title claims need a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar. Capacity should sit with title in this regime. Taking title under the general cap would put the core of what we are buying at risk.

### C. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance, and fraud
Applying the limitation, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance clauses to "all Claims of any nature" removes any fraud carve-out. The playbook requires carve-outs for fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and says no one may waive this. Counsel should confirm the enforceability position under NSW law, but the carve-out should be drafted in the SPA regardless.

### D. Disclosure and buyer knowledge (Sch 7, DL 1.1–1.2, 8.3)
Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers, and public searches would fix us with knowledge of nearly everything in the record. This is inconsistent with the playbook, which requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register, and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

Clause 8.3 pairs with this to bar claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable." That is a blanket knowledge bar, which the playbook says to delete. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities. Given that our due diligence has identified several of the issues below, a knowledge bar would undermine our protection on exactly the matters we have flagged.

### E. Bluefen (AUD 3.6m, ~30% FY26 revenue)
This is a material customer. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats consent as "satisfied on delivery." The playbook requires effective consent plus evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent. The disclosure confirms that no final written consent or evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room. This should be a condition precedent with documentary evidence.

### F. Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding as at September)
A post-Completion release is not acceptable. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only permitted with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval. The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. The balance needs refreshing.

### G. Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000 plus on-costs)
The funds flow excludes the bonuses and describes them as "a matter for the Seller." The playbook requires them to be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed in the disclosure and must be quantified and allocated. The conditions (Completion and continued employment) also need to be mapped to who bears the cost if they are not met.

### H. Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010, AUD 180,000)
The Seller's indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. The playbook requires broadening the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified; the disclosure states that DD-010 is not bank verification of non-payment. We should neither assume the amount is owed nor assume it is paid. Verification is needed.

### I. Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The record shows a download link sent to an unintended external address, possibly containing around 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps. Whether anyone accessed the file, the exact scope, and whether notification is required are all unknown. Under the playbook, we should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty, or numeric demand in either direction. We should not adopt the Seller's "not material" characterisation. We should require:
- preservation of logs;
- an investigation with defined scope;
- regular written updates until closure.

Whether to seek a specific indemnity for this matter is a judgement for the deal team, since the playbook sets out evidence and update requirements rather than a specific indemnity position. It should not be dismissed, given that the playbook says specific indemnities should never be excused by a knowledge qualifier.

### J. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
The Seller describes these as ordinary-course operating costs. The disclosure states they are not characterised as unavoidable, terminable, or accrued. Under the playbook, we should assess them. They should not be automatically treated as Debt or deducted from price.

### K. Tax and IP
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." The playbook says they remain open, with no unlimited liability assumed and no resolution. We should not accept that they are settled and should keep them in separate categories.

### L. Title (DD-012)
The share register is an internal Seller-supplied source. It does not establish title independently. The playbook requires independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances, and authority (for example, independent registry searches and a confirmation of the Seller's authority to sell).

### M. Other items
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The assignment restriction needs review. The disclosure does not confirm whether consent is required by a share sale. We need a written view on whether a change of control triggers the clause.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The notification obligation needs confirmation of whether landlord consent is required for the share sale.

---

## 3. Recommendations Summary

1. **Reject the Seller package as drafted.** Do not confirm it as acceptable or market standard.
2. **Hold the general cap at 25% / AUD 6m** and do not offer the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Reset thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
4. **Restore the 24-month general claims period.** Do not offer 18 months without Frost approval.
5. **Delete the "all claims" limitation override** and keep each category's regime separate.
6. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar. Include capacity.
7. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct** from all limitation, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
8. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure.** Reject data room, Accounts, register, and public-record deemed disclosure.
9. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (8.3).** Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.
10. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and satisfied conditions a pre-Completion requirement with documentary evidence. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
11. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
12. **Employee bonuses:** add AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or make them seller-funded.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 position independently.
14. **DD-006 incident:** require log preservation, a scoped investigation, and regular written updates. Assume no confirmed breach or loss in either direction. Consider whether a specific indemnity is warranted.
15. **Sandbar:** assess the three renewals on their terms. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
16. **Tax and IP:** keep open, reject "settled" characterisation, and do not assume unlimited liability or resolution.
17. **Title:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance, and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as internal only.
18. **Confirm with the Seller** whether Mossvale and the office lease require consent for the share sale.
19. **Refresh all facts** from the 22 September disclosure date before the mark-up is issued.

**Next steps:** Route any movement on the cap, time limit, or Riverlark/Bluefen conditions to Amelia Frost for authority. Each point should be reviewed by NSW-qualified counsel before the mark-up goes out.

1. **Reject the Seller package as drafted.** Do not confirm it as acceptable or market standard.
2. **Hold the general cap at 25% / AUD 6m** and do not offer the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Reset thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
4. **Restore the 24-month general claims period.** Do not offer 18 months without Frost approval.
5. **Delete the "all claims" limitation override** and keep each category's regime separate.
6. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis, and knowledge bar. Include capacity.
7. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct** from all limitation, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
8. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure.** Reject data room, Accounts, register, and public-record deemed disclosure.
9. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar (8.3).** Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.
10. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and satisfied conditions a pre-Completion requirement with documentary evidence. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
11. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. Post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
12. **Employee bonuses:** add AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or make them seller-funded.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 position independently.
14. **DD-006 incident:** require log preservation, a scoped investigation, and regular written updates. Assume no confirmed breach or loss in either direction. Consider whether a specific indemnity is warranted.
15. **Sandbar:** assess the three renewals on their terms. No automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
16. **Tax and IP:** keep open, reject "settled" characterisation, and do not assume unlimited liability or resolution.
17. **Title:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance, and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as internal only.
18. **Confirm with the Seller** whether Mossvale and the office lease require consent for the share sale.
19. **Refresh all facts** from the 22 September disclosure date before the mark-up is issued.

**Next steps:** Route any movement on the cap, time limit, or Riverlark/Bluefen conditions to Amelia Frost for authority. Each point should be reviewed by NSW-qualified counsel before the mark-up goes out.
